asof: Settles Tue 3 Nov 2026 · written Wed 4 Nov
headline: Hot JOLTS sells the strip 1.5–3.5bp, reds and greens lead; U7 peak at 4.545% still prices two hikes vs a one-hike Fed.
summary: The strip sold off across the board on Tuesday: Z6 and H7 rose 1.5bp in implied rate to 4.16% and 4.37%, M7 and U7 2bp to 4.505% and 4.545%, and Z7 through Z9 led with 3–3.5bp, more than reversing Monday's back-end rally. Month-to-date Z6 to U7 are 1.5–2.5bp higher and the reds 2.5–3bp higher, while U6 is barely changed and 2029 contracts are up 2–3bp. The peak is still SR3U7 at 4.545%, 59.5bp over the latest 3.95% SOFR fixing, with 13bp of easing priced from there to Z9. That is still about one hike more than the Fed's median and the consensus call of a December hike followed by a long hold.
drivers: Strong JOLTS reprices the labour market

September job openings jumped 333,000 to 7.523 million against about 7.10 million expected, August was revised up to 7.19 million, quits rose to 3.365 million and layoffs fell to 1.641 million. Two-year yields rose about 4.5bp to 4.63% and 10-year about 6bp to 4.95%; in SR3 Z6 and H7 rose 1.5bp and M7 and U7 2bp.
Reds cheapen into refunding and the vote

Z7 through Z9 sold off 3–3.5bp as the long end lost about 5.5bp ahead of Wednesday's refunding, where many dealers expect Treasury to loosen its steady-coupon guidance and lean more on bills and shorter notes, and as midterm results shape the fiscal outlook. Z6/Z7 widened 1.5bp to +36.5bp, while Z7/Z8 held at −8bp.
Oil slides again but no longer drives the strip

Brent hit $100.80 intraday on reports the US had approved a Qatari draft accord with Iran, then pared losses after Tehran said the US response fell short; WTI settled $0.37 lower at $96.09. Cheaper oil failed to stop the selloff, so the data, not energy, set Tuesday's direction.

SOFR fixed at 3.95% on 2 November, 7bp over the 3.88% EFFR and above the 3.90% interest on reserves, with reverse repo usage near $5bn. U6 at 3.925% implied, up only 0.2bp, still sits under the fixing.
spreads: The curve bear-steepened from the whites into the reds and then moved in parallel. U6/Z6 widened 1.3bp to +23.5bp, Z6/H7 held at +21bp, H7/M7 rose 0.5bp to +13.5bp and M7/U7 held at +4bp, while U7/Z7 rose 1bp to −2bp, so the peak stays in U7. Z6/Z7 widened 1.5bp to +36.5bp and Z6/M7 0.5bp to +34.5bp, 1bp wider on the month. Past the peak the inversion was little changed: Z7/Z8 flat at −8bp (0.5bp deeper month-to-date), U7/Z8 +1bp to −10bp and Z8/Z9 +0.5bp to −3bp. The H7/M7/U7 fly rose 0.5bp to +9.5bp (+1bp on the month) and M7/U7/Z7 fell 1bp to +6bp. Week- and month-to-date changes are the same, as both run from the 30 October settle.
fed: The latest fed funds futures snapshot is Monday's: 19.7bp for the 9 December meeting (a 79% chance of a hike), 25.5bp by January, 39.9bp by March, 55.1bp by June and a 59.5bp peak by September 2027 (implied EFFR 4.475%). That is up from 17.6bp, 24bp, 37.3bp, 52.1bp and 57bp at the 30 October month-end, but below 23.4bp, 32bp, 48.6bp, 66.3bp and 72bp a week earlier and well below 30.6bp, 43.5bp, 63.4bp and a 94bp peak at end-September. SR3 agrees at the peak: 4.475% plus SOFR's 7bp premium over EFFR is about 4.545%, level with U7 at 4.545%, while Z6 at 4.16% sits about 4.5bp under the January ZQ level plus that premium. Tuesday's 2-year selloff points to slightly firmer December pricing than Monday's snapshot. The strip still prices about two more hikes; the Fed's median projects one more this year and none in 2027, Logan has called for at least two, and payrolls on Friday (about 63,000 expected) and CPI on 10 November are the last big tests before December.

ideas.title: Sell the Z6/M7 calendar spread (fade 2027 hikes)
ideas.why: Open and 3.5bp in favour at +34.5bp, though it widened 0.5bp on Tuesday as M7 rose 2bp in rate against 1.5bp for Z6 after the hot JOLTS print. With 14.5bp to target and 5.5bp to the stop, reward is about 2.6 times risk. Kept: the ZQ peak of 59.5bp is down from 94bp at end-September and the Fed median sees one hike, not the extra 2027 move M7 still carries.
ideas.risk: A strong payrolls print on Friday or a hot CPI on 10 November could lift the 2027 hikes and push the spread back toward +40bp.

ideas.title: Buy 2028 easing: sell Z7, buy Z8
ideas.why: Open and flat at the −8bp entry after an unchanged day, as Z7 and Z8 both rose 3bp in implied rate. Only 11bp of easing is priced from Z7 to Z9; the target is 17bp away against 10bp to the stop, about 1.7 times. Kept at about half the core size: Tuesday's selloff was parallel through the reds and greens, so the easing story is intact, and a long-end-light refunding would help.
ideas.risk: If the refunding or midterm results add to term premium, or 2027 hikes keep coming out, the reds can flatten toward zero and push the spread through the stop.

ideas.title: Stay neutral the front contract through payrolls and refunding settlement

levels.Why neutral: fixings, not the Fed, drive it now

ideas.why: U6 settled at 3.925% implied, up 0.2bp on the day, while the latest 3.95% SOFR fixing sits 2.5bp above it and above the 3.90% interest on reserves. Refunding auctions next week and their mid-November settlement could keep repo firm, and only U6's final week sees the December decision; revisit after the 16 November settlement.
ideas.risk: If funding pressure fades quickly, SOFR could drop back to 3.88–3.90% and leave a couple of bp on the table.

watch: Any change to the steady-coupon guidance or a tilt to bills hits the reds and funding; ADP about 68,000 and ISM services about 54.8 expected.
Jobless claims; Q3 productivity and labour costs; Fed's Hammack, Barkin and Logan
Hammack dissented for a hike in October and Logan wants at least two more, so hawkish talk would support Z6/M7 wideners.
October payrolls; Fed's Williams and Bowman
About 63,000 expected after 29,000 with unemployment at 4.2%; the main test for Z6/M7, with Williams the key voice.
Brent and the US–Iran draft accord
Qatari mediators expect replies within about 36 hours; a deal would pull 2027 hikes lower, a breakdown would push them up.
The first refunding sale, $58bn if sizes are unchanged, tests front-end demand.
The last CPI before the December meeting after 3.7% in September; it sets Z6 and the December hike odds.
ZQ prices 19.7bp, a 79% chance of a hike; the outcome sets Z6 and the whites.
